title: The Parables of Jesus
description: Jesus taught the deepest truths with the simplest stories: a farmer sowing seed, a lost sheep, a runaway son, a stranger on the Jericho road, a mustard seed, three servants and two builders. Hear each parable from the King James Bible, what it meant to the people who first heard it, and what it asks of us now, with a prayer to close.

beats.say: He could have taught in riddles for scholars, or in laws for priests. Instead, Jesus told stories about farmers, shepherds, fathers, servants and seeds.
All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them.
A parable is a story with a door in it. You walk in thinking it is about someone else, and you walk out knowing it was about you. Let us walk through some of those doors together.
Behold, a sower went forth to sow. Seed was precious, and a farmer flung it wide by hand, across a field crossed by paths and stones and weeds.
Some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up. Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth, and sprang up fast, and withered in the sun.
Some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them. But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.
Jesus explained it himself. The thorns are the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, which choke the word. The seed is never the problem. The soil is.
Who hath ears to hear, let him hear. Ask yourself tonight which ground you are. And remember that soil can change: stones can be cleared, and thorns pulled up by the root.
The religious leaders muttered that Jesus welcomed sinners and ate with them. So he answered with three stories about lost things.
What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?
And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing. And he calls his friends: Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.
Or a woman with ten pieces of silver who loses one. Doth she not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?
There is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth. Heaven does not shrug at the lost. Heaven searches, and heaven throws a party.
A certain man had two sons. The younger said: Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. In that world, it was as good as saying: I wish you were dead.
He took the money to a far country, and wasted his substance with riotous living. When it was gone, a famine came, and he ended up feeding pigs, hungry enough to eat what they ate.
And when he came to himself, he said: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee.
But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him. A rich old man, running down the road.
Bring forth the best robe. For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
The older brother would not go in. Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine. The story ends with that door still open, for both sons, and for us.
A lawyer wanted to limit the commandment to love his neighbour. And who is my neighbour? Jesus answered with a story set on a dangerous road.
A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
A priest came by, and passed by on the other side. Then a Levite, and he too passed by on the other side. Both of them busy, both of them religious.
But a certain Samaritan, an outsider his hearers despised, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine.
He brought him to an inn, and took care of him, and paid for the rest. Which of these was neighbour unto him? Go, and do thou likewise.
The lawyer asked who he had to love. Jesus turned the question around: not who is my neighbour, but whose neighbour will I be? The answer is usually the person right in front of you.
His followers were few, poor, and unimpressive. So Jesus told them: The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field.
Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.
And another: The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened. Hidden, quiet, and unstoppable.
Small faith is not a failure. A whispered prayer, one kind act, one honest step: God starts things small on purpose, and grows them past what you can see.
A man travelling into a far country called his servants, and unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability.
The first two traded and doubled what they had been given. Their master said: Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things.
I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord. The reward for faithfulness was not rest. It was joy, and more to do.
The third said: I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth. Fear buried the gift. Whatever God has put in your hands, however small, do not bury it. Use it.

Notice that the master never asked for five from the man who was given two. He asked only for faithfulness with what each one had. That is all he asks of you: not someone else's gifts, just yours, used.
Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock.
And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.
The foolish man built upon the sand. The storm came to his house too, and it fell: and great was the fall of it.
Both men heard the same words. Both faced the same storm. The only difference was the doing. Faith is not proved in the sunshine. It is built there, and proved in the rain.

chapters.title: Two Men Went Up to Pray

beats.say: Two men went up into the temple to pray. One a Pharisee, respected and careful. The other a publican, a tax collector everyone despised.
The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself: God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.
And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying: God be merciful to me a sinner.
I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

chapters.title: A Prayer for Ears to Hear

beats.say: Let us pray. Lord Jesus, you told stories so that we would see ourselves in them. Show me where I am in your stories tonight.
Make me good ground. Clear the stones and pull up the thorns, the worries and the riches that choke your word in me.
When I am the lost son, bring me to myself and bring me home. When I am the older brother, open my heart to the party. When I see someone wounded on the road, do not let me pass by.
Help me to use what you have given me, and to build on the rock by doing what you say. God, be merciful to me a sinner. Amen.
